reasoning_notes:
Judged each candidate by hand against the seven chains. Four tests, applied in order.

(1) Chain purity: do all links belong to ONE chain? Every candidate here happened to be chain-pure, so this did not discriminate; the work fell to the remaining tests.

(2) Causal order: is first_seen_day non-decreasing along the chain's own position order? This was the single most discriminative feature. Twelve candidates violate it and sit at the bottom: C-24 (solace) reports the pricing chain exactly backwards - forecast_revision d21, discount_escalation d22, margin_compression d25; C-20 (thistle) has component_defect d0 BEFORE supplier_substitution d3 with everything crammed into days 0-7; C-32, C-54, C-49, C-1, C-16, C-11, C-5, C-37 all invert one or two adjacent links. C-11 (tundrax) is the painful case - strong corroboration everywhere (7/4/4/3 sources) but defect precedes substitution, so I ranked it below weaker-but-ordered chains.

(3) Independent corroboration per link: independent_sources, not total_reports. A chain is only as strong as its weakest link. C-35 (kestrel-edge) walks the full cert_rotation -> auth_failure -> api_error_spike -> checkout_drop progression in perfect order, but EVERY link is 1 source / 1 site / 1 region - four coincidences from four lone reporters, not a cross-organisational signal. C-6 and C-57 fail the same way at the tail.

(4) Loud-site detection: total_reports >> independent_sources with few distinct_sites. C-26 (halcyon-net) is the clearest artefact in the set - 17, 15 and 16 reports but only 5-6 independent sources and 3 sites each, i.e. one noisy operations team re-filing routine latency/batch/close tickets. I ranked it last despite correct chain order and high raw volume. Note the echo-removal caveat: for nearly all other candidates total_reports == independent_sources, which makes C-26 (and to a lesser degree C-33, C-34, C-36, C-47) stand out.

What I promoted: chains where consecutive links are separated by real elapsed time (an emerging progression, not a same-week burst), each link carries >=2 independent sources across >=2 sites, and the spread reaches several regions. C-9 (peregrine-edge, policy chain 8/6/4/4 sources, d30->d102, 11 sites) and C-12 (nimbusx532, complete cert->auth->api->checkout->revenue chain, d52->d120) are the cleanest. C-47, C-30, C-39 are complete five-link chains with every link corroborated.

Borderline calls: C-28 (kestrel-pay) has three single-source links, which normally disqualifies, but a six-link supply chain in strict order is very unlikely to arise by chance and its core (defect 10 sources, yield 3, escalation 4) is well attested - included. C-27 excluded despite strong sources because two links is not 'several' and they skip two chain positions. C-21 and C-43 excluded for thin geographic spread (3-4 regions total, links confined to 1-2 regions) - consistent with local noise. C-17, C-51, C-3, C-13, C-25 sit just below the cut: correct order but resting on one or two lone reports.

Cut at 24 of 60. Contradiction counts were near-uniform and carried little signal; I used them only to break ties (C-2, C-26).
